facts: The case involves two appeals preferred against the common judgment of the High Court of Judicature at Allahabad in Criminal Appeal No.749 of 1996 and Criminal Appeal No.761 of 1996 dated 1.10.2007.
The appellants are accused Nos.1 to 5, who were tried along with three other accused for alleged offences under Sections 147,148, 307 read with S.302 read with S.149 and S.452 of Indian Penal Code.

Sessions Court found accused Nos.6 to 8 not guilty of the charges and acquitted them, while convicted accused Nos.1 to 5 for the charge under S.302 read with S.149 IPC and sentenced them to death, subject to confirmation by the High Court.

The prosecution case is that on 13/14.7.1984, at about midnight Gurdip Singh heard firing and cries from the houses of Shisha Singh and Mohar Singh and armed with his licensed gun he along with Jassa Singh and Hazoor Singh moved towards the house of Shisha Singh.
The police party rushed to the place of occurrence and S.J. Mohd. Akhtar, S.O., Jhinjhana Police Station, took up the investigation and sent the injured to the hospital.
issues: Whether the conviction and sentence of accused Nos.1 to 5 are sustainable in law?
petitioner_arguments: Harbans Kaur is the sole eye-witness to the occurrence and her testimony is not reliable, as she named Surender Singh has fired gun shots at her and Surender, Mahender, Jinder who are sons of Kartar Singh were involved.

There is no motive attributable to the present appellants and it's a midnight occurrence and in the absence of effective source of light it is doubtful as to whether the witness could have recognized the assailants.
respondent_arguments: Harbans Kaur was seriously injured in the occurrence and only one question was asked by the Magistrate as to who caused injury to her and in her reply she named Surender Singh and the other sons of Kartar Singh.
After gaining full consciousness in her statement given before the Investigation Officer, she has narrated the entire occurrence and the names of all the accused.
court_reasoning: The Court held that Harbans Kaur's testimony is reliable as it was consistent with the FIR which came into being immediately after the occurrence based on the complaint given by Sardar Gurdip Singh.
The motive for the occurrence was established, as Harbans Kaur is the wife of Shisha Singh and the dwelling house of Mohar Singh was adjacent to her house.
holding: The Court allowed the appeals and remitted the matter back to the High Court for reconsideration.
